Estimates are calculated from figures which are as reported by police. Since 2016, changes in severity reporting systems for a large number of police forces mean that serious injury figures, and to a lesser extent slight injuries, are not comparable with earlier years. The adjustment has now been rolled out across the annual publication, and incorporated  to the mid-year estimation method. Columns may not add up to 100 per cent as casualties are from collisions which can have more than one road safety factor.

As of 2024, a significant portion of the road safety factor data was directly recorded using the new road safety factor system. For the remaining collisions, the data was collected using the contributory factor system and converted to road safety factors, either in police systems or by DfT. Analysis of the collisions natively recorded as road safety factors has shown that there is a step change in which factors are being recorded, compared to the data that has been converted from contributory factors. Percentage results are presented separately in this workbook and caution should be exercised in making any comparisons between data converted from contributory factors and those recorded directly as road safety factors. Data collected using the contributory factor system is referred to as "converted", whilst data originally collected as road safety factors is referred to as "directly recorded".
